page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD processor architecture and features a constrained vCPU profile. Specifically, it exposes 2 dedicated vCPUs while retaining access to the memory and I/O footprint typically assigned to larger 8-vCPU host slots within the Eadsv7 family.

Hardware allocation includes 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a high memory density of 32.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture incorporates 472 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, providing fast ephemeral storage, and the instance supports Premium Storage configurations. No discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs are included, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly.

This server profile delivers an extreme memory-to-core ratio of 32:1, significantly exceeding standard memory-optimized tiers. The trade-off is focused computational throughput: with only 2 dedicated vCPUs, intensive multi-threaded workloads will face execution bottlenecks, but applications licensed on a per-core basis gain substantial cost efficiency by minimizing core counts while retaining 64.0 GB of memory and fast local scratch space.

Azure E8-2ads_v7 is tailored for workloads requiring significant RAM footprints and local scratch disk speed without needing high compute parallelization. It is well suited for database engines with core-based licensing, in-memory caching tiers such as Redis or Memcached, and memory-intensive data processing or ETL staging pipelines.
